blocks.p: Gin's chapter on the Grid began with a journal note written between two cases, and Rei could hear his brother's tired, pleased voice in every line. It was the only chapter in the archive that Gin said he had looked forward to writing. Rei read it at the kitchen table until the windows went grey.

doc.title: Gin's preface, Chapter 17. The Grid
lines: No hierarchy. No building. No official anything.
The Grid is not an organization. There is no Grid leadership. There are no Grid membership fees or registration requirements or official anything.

The Grid works because the people in it learned the same things from the same hard lessons and arrived at the same conclusions independently. What looks like coordination from outside is actually convergence.
This is the part of this work that I trust most completely and have described least.
G.U. Keys on the hook.

doc.title: Grid Intelligence Reference. What The Grid Is
lines: A network of people who owe each other things and who have collectively decided that owing each other things is preferable to owing the CVD things.
I have found this network more reliable in field emergencies than the official support system approximately seventy percent of the time.

Joining the Grid is not a process. Someone in the Grid vouches for you to another person in the Grid. That person gives you one thing, a contact, an address, a piece of information you needed. If you handle it correctly, you get another contact.
If you handle it incorrectly, the network closes around you and the contacts stop. That is the entirety of the Grid's enforcement mechanism.

blocks.p: Rei thought of the room above the shuttered shop, and of the man who had given him that address, and of the node who had vouched for him to the man. One contact, then another. He had been handling it, he realised, without knowing there was anything to handle.

doc.title: Grid Culture. The Unwritten Rules That Everyone Knows
lines: Show up. If you say you will be somewhere, be there. Unreliability in entity work produces casualties rather than inconveniences.
Don't bring heat. Do not draw CVD attention to Grid locations, contacts or supply chains. Do not compromise a safe house.
Share what matters. Information that could help someone avoid harm is shared without being asked. The network is not gossip. It is operational infrastructure.
Debt and reciprocity. When someone helps you, you help someone else. The timeline is flexible. The obligation is not.

Protect practitioners in danger. You will not be left alone in the situations the official framework cannot or will not address. This promise is kept imperfectly and kept more often than any institutional equivalent.

doc.title: Margin, G.U.
lines: The extraction in Chapter 8. A Channel rank Psychometabolic the CVD had filed an acquisition order on. Eleven days, four practitioners, clean exit. No authorization, no cover, no pay.

The CVD will tell you the Grid is disorganised. It is not disorganised. It is organised the way water is... around obstacles, by relationship, with no centre to seize. A thing it cannot decapitate, because it has no head.

blocks.p: Rei read the fourth rule again. The timeline is flexible. The obligation is not. It was the same word the widow had used without knowing it. Debt. But the Grid's debt moved. It went from one person to the next and never came back to the same hand. The Healer's debt only ran one way, toward the Healer.

doc.title: The Infrastructure. Safe Houses
lines: Locations maintained by Grid-adjacent practitioners or civilians who understand the work. From a spare room to a dedicated space.

Standard warding on the entrance, at minimum. A practitioner who built the safe house typically inks at least the threshold. A supply cache, food, water, first aid for physical and veil-adjacent injury. Some form of communication that does not run through institutional channels. The contact information for the next node.
Finding them. By vouch only. A safe house compromised is a safe house gone.

In this district. Four safe houses documented in my Grid network file. Locations, warding status, supply levels, and contact practitioners are in the Grid intelligence file on page 147. I check them every three months.

The safe house I use most often is run by a retired practitioner who left the CVD registration system twelve years ago. She is 61, older than almost any active practitioner I know, and has been doing this for forty years without institutional support. Her ward configurations are the most sophisticated I have encountered outside Tower Family property. I have learned more about practical symbol work from her than from any formal source.
Her name is not in this archive. The file on page 147 has the names.

blocks.p: Rei turned to page 147. He knew it already. It was where Gin had written down the four nodes, the baker, the clinic behind the blue curtain, the café that kept Tuesday evenings free, the shrine room behind the Korean restaurant. He had read the page a dozen times this week. This time he read the bottom of it, where under the four names there was a short note in Gin's smallest hand. It described a place in words rather than an address, the way a person gives directions to a friend who already knows the neighbourhood. It did not name the place. It assumed the reader would know how to find it. Rei read it four times and did not yet know. He marked the page with the corner of a receipt and kept going.

doc.title: Supply Networks. The Black Market for Practitioner Materials
lines: Prepared binding materials, silver-adjacent ammunition, stability supplies the CVD controls, ink and substrate for tattoo configurations, materials for high-grade seals, modified medical supplies for Psychometabolic field work.

No Grid warehouse. The Psychometabolic who prepares field medical kits sends them through three contacts before they reach the practitioner who needs them. The distribution is inefficient by design. Each link in the chain knows only the link immediately before and after it.
Payment. A mix of money and reciprocal obligation. Practitioners who can pay do, and practitioners who cannot are carried by the network until they can.
The ammunition preparation contact in this district. The silver rounds they produce are the most consistent I have used in six years. I will not document their name or location here.

doc.title: The Information Network
lines: Person to person, weighted by trust. No quality control except the reputation of the person sharing.
The Grid's information network has no archive. When a practitioner with significant knowledge retires, relocates, or dies, their accumulated intelligence goes with them.
The Satō case is a good example. Eleven years of accumulated entity intelligence about the Kita district entity, held in one practitioner's memory and then in a fragment in an absorber.
This archive is, among other things, an attempt to address the information preservation problem for my own accumulated knowledge. I built it for one person.

blocks.p: I built it for one person. Rei put his hand flat on the page. The kitchen was very quiet.

blocks.cap: Who joins the Grid, and why

doc.title: Who Joins The Grid And Why
lines: Unregistered practitioners, who did not know registration was available or chose not to register.
Registration gap practitioners, whose registered rank does not match what they can actually do. Some suppressed on registration to stay out of the pipeline.
CVD graduates who left.
Specialised practitioners, such as high-grade mediums and people with entity relationships the CVD would call violations.
I am a registered CVD practitioner who is also Grid-affiliated. My suppression keeps the extent of my Grid work invisible. I am probably not even unusual.

blocks.cap: How the Grid teaches, one person to another

doc.title: How the Grid teaches. G.U.
lines: The Grid does not recruit. Nobody hands you the Grid. You are let into it one person at a time, by being the sort of person someone is willing to be wrong about.

It teaches through direct teaching relationships. Its symbol work is held in practitioners, not documents. Its greatest advantage over the CVD is post-possession recovery. It has handled far more possession recoveries than the official record shows, because most of them were never reported.

My first Grid contact was a practitioner I met at a possession case the CVD had closed as resolved when it was not resolved. She was doing the actual clearance work after the official case was closed. She did not explain what the Grid was. She just worked the case and let me help. Three months later she called me for a case I was needed on. That was the beginning of six years of network.
The vouch is a serious thing. When someone vouches for you, they extend their own reliability to cover yours. If you fail, they fail with you.
Find your people inside it. The ones who will sit with you after the difficult work. They are in there. Find them.

blocks.p: Rei closed the archive with the receipt still marking page 147. Post-possession recovery. Somewhere in this city were people who had brought someone back from where Gin was now, and who had never written it down. And somewhere, in the place on that page, there was a woman of sixty-one with the best ward configurations in Tokyo, who had taught his brother how to draw a threshold. Rei did not know her name. He knew, now, that Gin had left him a way to find it.
